name: fig_lean_z3_performance
title: Lean 4 and Z3 runtime vs problem size
question: How do verification (Lean) and solver (Z3) runtimes scale with the number of experiment x configuration pairs?
model: Wall-clock timing (time.perf_counter) of lean_runner.check_batch, smt.evaluate, smt.rank_alternatives and scripts/build_grid.py on the same pairs.
caption: Measured runtime of the Lean 4 checker (decides every verdict) and Z3 (explains and ranks) against problem size on a 32-CPU machine. Medians of 5 runs (3 runs for Z3 at 1000 pairs); bars span min to max. Lean check_batch in one process: 5000 pairs in 4.83 s (0.97 ms/pair). Z3 evaluate, serial: 1000 pairs in 7.0 s (7.0 ms/pair). Full grid (44,880 pairs, scripts/build_grid.py, 24 worker processes, including serialisation and database writes): median 51 s over 3 runs. Z3 was not run on the full grid and no extrapolation is drawn.
